# PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] `find_one()` returns the first matching document as a Python dictionary, or `None` when no document matches. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/find.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/collection.html
- [statement] Call `close()` when abandoning a cursor early, or use `with collection.find() as cursor:` so the cursor closes when the block ends. Exhausted ordinary cursors close automatically. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/cursors.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/collection.html
- [statement] Client-level operation models need a namespace: the `InsertOne` implementation rejects a missing namespace when adding an operation to a client bulk. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-python-driver/blob/main/pymongo/operations.py
- [statement] Cursors return read results in iterable batches and hold a subset of the documents in memory; this supports processing large results incrementally. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/cursors.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/find.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use `insert_one()` for one document and `insert_many()` for a list of documents. The driver generates an `ObjectId` for a missing `_id`; explicitly supplied `_id` values must be unique within the collection. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/insert.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Use `limit()`, `sort()`, and `skip()` to shape query results. When combined, the driver applies sort and skip before limit regardless of the order of these method calls. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/specify-documents-to-return.md
- [statement] A cursor is not a Python list. Each index access or slice runs a new query using skip and limit, so iterating with repeated `cursor[idx]` accesses is inefficient and can produce surprising results. (low confidence) — https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/cursor.html
- [statement] For collection bulk writes, `ordered` defaults to `True`: the driver preserves operation order and skips remaining operations after an individual write error. With `ordered=False`, the driver attempts all individual writes in arbitrary order and reports write errors after those attempts. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/bulk-write.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/crud/bulk-write.md
- [statement] Unordered client bulk writes still stop on a top-level error such as a network or command error; continuing after an individual write error does not guarantee completion after communication failure. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/crud/bulk-write.md
- [statement] Collection bulk failures use `BulkWriteError`, whose `details` includes failure information. Client bulk failures use `ClientBulkWriteException`; its `error` describes top-level failure and can be absent for individual write failures. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/bulk-write.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-python-driver/blob/main/pymongo/errors.py
- [statement] A client bulk exception can expose `partial_result`, containing successful operations performed before the error. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-python-driver/blob/main/pymongo/errors.py
- [statement] Collection `bulk_write()` defaults to `ordered=True`: requests execute serially in the provided order, and a write error aborts remaining operations. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/bulk-write.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/collection.html
- [statement] The bulk-write guide’s introductory failure paragraph says a collection write failure stops further operations. Its unordered section and the collection API qualify this: unordered bulk writes attempt all operations. Read the introductory stop statement in the context of ordered execution. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/bulk-write.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/collection.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] `find()` returns matching documents through a cursor; iterate it with a `for` loop so the application can process results in batches rather than retain the complete result set. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/find.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/cursors.md
- [statement] `find()` accepts a query filter and returns a cursor; an empty filter selects all documents. Iterate the cursor with a `for` loop instead of materializing the entire result. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/find.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/collection.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The synchronous CRUD examples use `update_one()` or `update_many()` with a query filter and a `$set` update document, `replace_one()` with a replacement document, and `delete_one()` or `delete_many()` with a query filter. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud.md
- [statement] Converting a cursor with `list(results)` retrieves all its documents into application memory. The cursor guide warns that results exceeding available memory can crash the program and recommends iterative access for large results. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/query/cursors.md
- [statement] The documented minimums for `MongoClient` bulk operations are PyMongo v4.9 and MongoDB Server v8.0. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/bulk-write.md
- [statement] `Collection.bulk_write()` returns `BulkWriteResult`, with inserted, deleted, matched, modified and upserted counts; `upserted_ids` maps operation indexes to the inserted `_id` values. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/languages/python/pymongo-driver/current/crud/bulk-write.md · keywords: PyMongo CRUD API, cursors and bulk_write · also: https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/collection.html
- [statement] The driver bulk-write specification records write-concern errors without terminating bulk execution solely for that reason, then requires an exception at the end if any occurred. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/crud/bulk-write.md
- [statement] `projection` restricts the returned fields. In the collection API, a list projection always includes `_id`; use a mapping to exclude `_id`. (low confidence) — https://pymongo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/pymongo/collection.html
